title: 24 Hours in Lisbon: Custard Tarts, Hills and Sunsets
creator: Ines on the Road
description:
Day one in Lisbon! Belém, Alfama, two miradouros and way too many pastéis de nata.

sentences.t: Good morning from Lisbon!
It is seven a.m., and I'm up early because I have one goal today, and it's to get to Pastéis de Belém before the line wraps around the block.
Spoiler, I did not make it before the line.
But it moves fast, maybe fifteen minutes.
And honestly, the custard tarts are worth it, they come out warm and you dust the cinnamon on top yourself.
I had three.
I'm not going to apologize for that.
After that we walked over to the Jerónimos Monastery, which is right next door.
The cloister is unreal, every column is carved differently, ropes and sea creatures and little faces.
Get there right when it opens if you can, because by eleven it's packed with tour groups.
From Belém we took the tram, the fifteen, back toward the center.
Everyone talks about tram twenty-eight, and yes, it's charming, but it is also basically a sardine can full of tourists and pickpockets.
My tip is to ride it really early or really late, or just walk the route, it's all hills anyway.
Speaking of hills, Lisbon will destroy your calves.
Wear real shoes, because the sidewalks are these polished limestone tiles, and when they're wet they're like ice.
I saw two people slip today, and one of them was me.
For lunch we went to a tiny place in Alfama with no menu, the owner just tells you what's cooking.
Today it was grilled sardines, boiled potatoes, and a salad, plus a jug of house wine, and the whole thing was like fourteen euros.
After lunch we wandered around Alfama with no plan, which is the best way to do it.
You get lost, you climb some stairs, and you end up at a viewpoint you didn't know existed.
This one is Miradouro de Santa Luzia, and look at those orange rooftops going all the way down to the river.
Then sunset at Miradouro da Senhora do Monte, which is the highest viewpoint in the city.
Bring a drink, everybody else does, and there's usually someone with a guitar.
Dinner was at Time Out Market, which locals kind of roll their eyes at.
But if you're tired and everyone wants something different, it's perfect.
I got a steak sandwich called a prego, and it was so good I'm thinking about it right now.
So that was day one in Lisbon.
Tomorrow we're doing a day trip to Sintra, and I've been told to book the palace tickets ahead, so I'm doing that tonight.
Thanks so much for watching, and if you've been to Lisbon, leave your favorite spot in the comments.
See you in Sintra!
